title: SpecFit: Not All Draft Tokens Cost the Same in Offloaded MoE Inference
abstract: arXiv:2610.15417v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models activate only a few experts per token, but when their expert weights are offloaded to host memory, host-to-device (H2D) expert transfers enter the critical path of decoding. Speculative decoding verifies several draft tokens in one forward pass, yet in an MoE model each verified token activates its own experts, so a larger draft tree transfers more experts. Because of this H2D cost, speculative decoding commits several tokens per verification cycle yet is sometimes even slower than autoregressive decoding. Based on this observation, we propose SpecFit, which chooses the verified draft subtree to maximize predicted throughput rather than acceptance length. SpecFit estimates the expected number of committed tokens from draft path probabilities and predicts cycle time from the node count and the per-layer union of the experts the subtree activates; this union is a monotone submodular coverage function, so eac

tldr: 针对卸载式MoE推理中投机解码因专家传输开销反而变慢的问题，SpecFit通过联合建模token接受概率与专家传输成本，选择最大化预测吞吐量的草稿子树进行验证，从而实现更快的解码。
en_tdlr: SpecFit speeds up offloaded MoE inference by selecting the draft subtree that maximizes predicted throughput—jointly accounting for token acceptance and expert transfer costs—rather than simply maximizing acceptance length.
